summary: Govind Swamirao Gai (1917–1995) worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He served as Chief Epigraphist for the Government of India (attested 1958–1966), Chief Epigraphist for India at the Archaeological Survey of India (1966–1976), and consultant for epigraphy at AIIS (attested 1986).

Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt was an Indology scholar who taught Arunoday Natvarlal Jani. He served as a professor at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (attested 1933–1939) and as director of the Oriental Institute, Baroda (attested 1953–1957).

Grace S. Fong (born 1948) is a sinologist who studied at McGill University and the University of British Columbia (~1974–1984). She served as professor at Smith College (~1985–1989) and as associate professor and department chair at McGill University (~1992).

Graeme MacQueen (1948–2023) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who earned his doctorate at Harvard University (~1971–1979) under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He served as a lecturer at McMaster University (~1977–2003).

Grafton Elliot Smith (1871–1937) was a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Sydney, Sydney Medical School (~1888–1892), and St John's College (~1896–1899), later holding a post at University College London (~1919–1936).

Graham E. Clarke (died 1998) was a scholar in Tibetology and other fields. He held posts at the Institute of Development Studies and at the University of Oxford, where he was attested as a senior member in 1998.
Graham Lock is a scholar in the fields of linguistics and Buddhist studies. He studied under Hsuan Hua and Saddhaloka Bhikkhu.

Graham Priest (born 1948) works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Educated at Cambridge and the LSE under John Lane Bell, he held posts at the University of Melbourne (~2000–2009), University of St Andrews (~2007–2018), and CUNY Graduate Center (~2009).

Graves Chamney Haughton (1788–1849) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Fort William College. He co-founded and served as secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society and was Professor of Hindú Literature at East India Company College (1819–1827).

Gray Tuttle works in Tibetology, Sinology, and history. He earned his Ph.D. at Harvard (-2002) under William C. Kirby, Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp, and Philip A. Kuhn, later becoming professor and department chair at Columbia University.

Graziadio Isaia Ascoli (1829–1907) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He served as a professor at the Accademia Scientifico-Letteraria di Milano from 1861 to 1902 and founded the Archivio Glottologico Italiano in 1873.

Greg Bailey (born 1948) is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under J. Durham and Madeleine Biardeau. He served as a professor at La Trobe University, where his posts were attested in 1994 and 2004.

Gregor Ahn (born 1958) studied at Copenhagen and Bonn, completing his PhD and Habilitation under Hans-Joachim Klimkeit. Working in religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies, he taught at Münster, Tartu, and served as professor at Heidelberg University (1996–2025).

Gregory Adam Scott is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history who studied at Columbia University. His posts include Dr at the University of Edinburgh (attested 2026) and Senior Lecturer at the University of Manchester (attested 2026).

Gregory Forgues is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna (attested 2011) under Helmut Tauscher, and studied under Birgit Kellner as well as several traditional teachers.

Gregory Hillis is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed an MA at the University of Virginia (-1993), where he also held a post (attested 2002), and is a continuing lecturer at UC Santa Barbara (attested 2026).

Gregory Max Seton is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned degrees from Naropa University, UC Santa Barbara (-2008), and a D.Phil from the University of Oxford (-2015), where he was supervised by Vesna Wallace and Alexis Sanderson.

Gregory P. A. Levine (born 1963) is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history. He studied at Oberlin College and Princeton University, and became an Associate Professor of Art History at the University of California, Berkeley (~2003).

Gregory Price Grieve (born 1964), a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies, earned his degrees from SFSU and the University of Chicago. He taught at Chicago and DePaul before becoming Professor and Department Head at UNC Greensboro in 2002.

Gregory Schopen (born 1947) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. at ANU under Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana. He held professorships at Indiana University, UT Austin, and UCLA (1999–2019).
